props.title: A request, not a rule
props.md: "Claude reads it and tries to follow it, but there's no guarantee of strict compliance, especially for vague or conflicting instructions." (Claude Code docs)

props.title: Get a first draft
props.ask: Read this folder and draft a short CLAUDE.md for it. Don't save it until I've read it.
props.expect: Claude looks around, then shows you a draft. Cut anything vague, add what it couldn't know, then let it save.

steps.title: A clear desk
steps.text: Each Claude Code **session** starts with a fresh context window, without the conversation from last time. Think of a temp who starts fresh every morning: capable, but new to your project.

steps.title: The note, read first
steps.text: **CLAUDE.md** is a plain text file in your project folder. Claude Code reads it at the start of every session, before your first message, like a handover note left on the temp's desk.

steps.title: What goes in
steps.text: Write down what you'd otherwise explain every time: what the folder is, how to run things, the words you use, your preferences. Be concrete: "never edit files in data/raw" works better than "be careful with the data".

steps.title: Keep it short
steps.text: The note stays on the desk all session, so every line takes room. Claude Code's docs suggest under 200 lines: longer files take more space and are followed less reliably. Keep a long manual in its own file and mention it by name: Claude opens it only when it decides a task needs it.

steps.title: It survives compaction
steps.text: When the desk fills, older conversation is boiled down into a summary: **compaction**. Instructions you only gave in chat can get lost, but the project's CLAUDE.md is re-read from disk and put back whole.

steps.title: /init writes a draft
steps.text: Type `/init` in Claude Code: Claude looks through the folder and writes a starting CLAUDE.md. If one already exists, it suggests improvements instead of overwriting it. Then add what Claude couldn't discover on its own.

steps.title: A request, not a rule
steps.text: Claude treats CLAUDE.md as context, not enforced settings: it usually follows it, which is probabilistic, not certain. When something must happen every time, a **hook** turns the request into a rule (see C5, *Hooks*).

steps.title: The whole picture
steps.text: A short note, read at the start of every session and again after compaction, carries your standing instructions from one clear desk to the next. Keep it brief and concrete, and let hooks handle what must be certain.
